before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}x-1, & x<0.5 \\ 4-{x}^{2}, & x\ge 0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

- $(0,1)$
- $[0,2]$
- $[1,2]$
before.html:

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

decision.explanation: The extreme value theorem requires continuity on a closed, bounded interval. I is not closed. II contains x=0.5, where the left-hand limit is -0.5 but f(0.5)=3.75, so the function is discontinuous. On III, f(x)=4-x^2 is continuous throughout [1,2]. Thus only III qualifies.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}x-1, & x<0.5 \\ 4-{x}^{2}, & x\ge 0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

- $(0,1)$
- $[0,2]$
- $[1,2]$
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- The interval $(0,1)$ is not closed, so the extreme value theorem is not applicable.

- Now, consider $[0,2].$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0.5}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0.5}(x-1)=(0.5)-1=-0.5, \\ {lim}_{x\to {0.5}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0.5}(4-{x}^{2})=4-(0.5)^{2}=3.75.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits from the left and from the right of $x=0.5$ are not the same. Hence, $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=0.5.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[0,2],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

- Finally, consider $[1,2].$ The only discontinuity of the function $f(x)$ is at $x=0.5,$ which is not in the interval $[1,2].$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $[1,2],$ and the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "III only".

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1), & x>1 \\ x-1, & x\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

- $[0,2]$
- $[-1,0]$
- $[-1,2]$
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- First, consider $[0,2].$ In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)=-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x)$ has an essential discontinuity at $x=1.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[0,2],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

- Now, consider the interval $[-1,0].$ In this interval, $f(x)=x-1$ and so $f(x)$ is continuous on $[-1,0].$  Therefore, the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

- Finally, in the interval $[-1,2]$, we also have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)=-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 
Hence, $f(x)$ is not continuous on $[-1,2]$ and therefore  the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "II only".
